title: Venture
description: One venture: anything a builder undertakes, from a hobby to a company (EE-011). Each venture keeps a venture.json at its root, beside its venture profile. Its products are cards in products/, the parties it keeps records for are accounts in accounts/ (optional, EE-021), and ventures can hold ventures. Cross-venture rules are checked by schema/check-ventures.mjs. Nouns follow docs/ontology.md (EE-014).

kind.description: venture: building a venture, whose root and strategic foundation fail closed. product: a product without a venture, which fails open (EE-054).

parent.description: The id of the venture that holds this one; null at the top of a workspace.

phase.description: How far the venture has come (EE-012). discovery: does a real problem exist, and who has it. validation: will people adopt this solution and keep using it. beachhead: can it win one segment repeatably at a profitable cost. scale: how fast can it take the mass market. platform: what will others build on. Gates and references: purpose/frameworks/product-anatomy/phases.json.

ambition.description: Why the venture exists and how far through the phases it means to go. hobby follows the IRS sense: not engaged in for profit.

form.description: Whether and how the venture is formalized.

industry.description: What the venture produces, by its current flagship. Re-checked at each phase gate.

system.description: NAICS (North American Industry Classification System), production-oriented

core.description: The core product (Product Anatomy): what anyone can claim from this venture. Required once the venture leaves discovery.

must_not.description: What it must never deliver under its name

competence.description: The core competence that makes the promise deliverable (Prahalad and Hamel)

departments.description: The departments this venture imports, by id from operations/departments.json (EE-047). Only these get folders; the rest are not in the venture at all until need-now suggests them and the builder adds them (EE-048).

packages.description: The Naive packages this venture uses, by name from packages/ (EE-071), the way package.json lists dependencies (Next.js translation P-3). Left out, the manifest derives them: the core packages that fit the phase now plus any package holding records. Checked by schema/structure.mjs.

kits.description: The Mentura kits this venture uses (EE-071). Each names the one package it extends, which the venture must use; the kit itself lives on the platform.

functions.description: The venture's functions and their one accountable owner each (EE-071), keyed by function id from operations/departments.json. A solo founder owns them all, which is what the manifest assumes when this is left out.

owner.description: A role or a person's name; no personal details

brand.description: The venture's verbal brand elements, owned by the brand pillar. Visual identity (tokens, logos) is a separate record.

tagline.description: The brand's enduring short line, kept across campaigns (Burger King's 'Have it your way'). A campaign's slogan is not this; it belongs to the campaign.

members.description: The others who work in the venture, by role, people and agents alike: a string role (co-founder, partner, investor) or an object naming the kind. No personal details. Any member switches on governance, since agents need decision rights too.

role.description: A role id from the roles register (builder, architect) or a plain role

tools.description: For agents: the interfaces or runtimes it runs in (integration ids)

profile.description: Path to the venture profile (Markdown): narrative, pillars and changelog.

layers.description: Every venture has the same six layers (execution folded into operations, EE-038), at the depth it needs. A layer not used yet is false.

links.description: What crosses from this venture into another, one way.

repos.description: The venture's repositories (repo is short for repository): version-controlled stores, normally Git, holding code and the documents that ship with it (docs-as-code). The venture folder itself lives in the vault. A venture that builds software needs at least one; ventures in other industries may need none (EE-020)

location.description: Path relative to the workspace's code folder

products.description: Product ids whose code it holds

regulation.description: How much laws, regulators or formal standards constrain what the venture may do (EE-040; MAD's governance tier reads it as regulatory_exposure). The obligations themselves are founder decisions made with counsel.

exposure.description: light: ordinary terms of service and licences. some: obligations such as personal data, accessibility rules or industry codes. heavy: health, finance, safety-critical or government work, where an auditor or regulator must be satisfied.

regimes.description: The laws, regulators or standards that apply, such as GDPR, HIPAA or SOC 2

location.description: Folder path, relative to the folder that holds venture.json
